EQUITY AND HUMAN RELATIONS COMMISSION AGENDA
  WEDNESDAY, MARCH 4, 2026
  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 6:00 PM

Christopher Covington, Chair  Cheryl Koll, Commissioner
Jon Schultz, Vice Chair  Dr. Eduardo Lara, Commissioner
Richard Brown, Commissioner  M. Lissette Flores, Commissioner
Robbie Butler, Commissioner  Keyona Montgomery, Commissioner
Joshua De Leon, Commissioner  Nolan Ross Samé-Weil, Commissioner
Ricky Dockery, Commissioner  Benita Shaw-Malone, Commissioner

  Equity and Human Relations Commission In-Person Meeting

  Members of the public have the option to submit online and email public comments
  to tony.viramontes@longbeach.gov

  Comments may also be provided in the Zoom meeting using the raise hand function or by
  pressing *9 on your phone

  Please dial: (213) 338-8477 / Meeting ID: 999 5379 6768
  https://longbeach-gov.zoom.us/j/99953796768

  Please note the Zoom meeting may encounter technical disruptions, but in-person access
  and public comment will continue to be available in accordance with the Brown Act

  To view the meeting from your computer, tablet, or smartphone
  visit: https://longbeach.primegov.com/public/portal?fromiframe=true

CALL TO ORDER

ROLL CALL

CHAIR REMARKS

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  26-54487  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Equity and Human Relations
  Commission meeting of Wednesday, February 4, 2026.

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

2.  26-54502  Recommendation to review, discuss, and, if appropriate, approve the transmittal of
  a letter from the Federal Immigration Enforcement Ad Hoc Committee to the City
  Council, outlining policy recommendations related to federal immigration
  enforcement and its impacts on equity and human relations in Long Beach.

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 6:00 PM

3.  26-54503  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation on the Disability Data and

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

4.  26-54504  Recommendation to receive and file a report from current Ad Hoc Committees;
  discuss anticipated Ad Hoc Committees for upcoming projects; and, if appropriate,

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

PUBLIC COMMENT

Opportunity to address the Equity and Human Relations Commission on non-agenda items. Each
speaker is limited to three minutes to make their comments unless extended by the Chair.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

ADJOURNMENT

I, Alyssa Campos, City Clerk Specialist, certify that the agenda was posted not less than 72 hours
prior to the meeting.

NOTE: The agenda and supporting documents are available online at
https://longbeach.gov/cityclerk/meetings. If a special accommodation is desired pursuant to the
Americans with Disabilities Act, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 570-6101 or
cityclerk@longbeach.gov.

  FINISHED AGENDA & MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

At 6:10 PM, Chair Covington called the meeting to order.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present: Butler, De Leon, Dockery, Lara, Lissette Flores, Montgomery, Samé-
Weil, Schultz, Covington

Commissioners Absent: Brown, Koll, Shaw-Malone

Also present: Teresa Chandler, Deputy City Manager, Alanah Grant, Equity Officer,
Tony Viramontes, Equity and Community Engagement Program Specialist, Atoy Wilson, Deputy City
Attorney, Alyssa Campos, City Clerk Specialist, Rosa Garibay, City Clerk Assistant.

Commissioner Brown, Commissioner Koll, and Commissioner Shaw-Malone were excused from the
meeting.

CHAIR REMARKS

Commissioner Samé-Weil provided a land acknowledgment.

 Chair Covington provided opening remarks.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  26-54487  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Equity and Human Relations
  Commission meeting of Wednesday, February 4, 2026.

  A motion was made by Vice Chair Schultz, seconded by Commissioner Samé-
  Weil, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8 Butler, De Leon, Dockery, Lissette Flores, Montgomery, Samé-Weil,
  Schultz, Covington
  No:  0 None

2.  26-54502  Recommendation to review, discuss, and, if appropriate, approve the transmittal of
  a letter from the Federal Immigration Enforcement Ad Hoc Committee to the City
  Council, outlining policy recommendations related to federal immigration
  enforcement and its impacts on equity and human relations in Long Beach.

  A motion was made by Vice Chair Schultz, seconded by Commissioner Lara,
  to approve recommendation, as amended, to make the following updates to
  the letter: [1] under Section 2, add Long Beach City College and California
  State University, Long Beach to the list of Task Force representatives; [2]
  under Section 4, update the first funding strategy bullet point to state,
  “Identification of ongoing budget allocations and goals necessary to sustain
  legal defense, rapid response, training, compliance monitoring, and data
  governance;” and [3] under Section 5, update the first sentence to state,
  “Build upon the City’s existing Data Privacy Guidelines by adopting enhanced
  Citywide data and artificial intelligence (AI) minimization, governance, and
  accountability standards designed to reduce unnecessary exposure of
  sensitive information and strengthen lawful data stewardship”. The
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9 Butler, De Leon, Dockery, Lara, Lissette Flores, Montgomery, Samé-
  Weil, Schultz, Covington
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
